coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel D
record.summary: Phase 1 residential parcel between Building 2 and the new 21st Street, 90 ft under the D4D, designed by Stanley Saitowitz | Natoma Architects as an L-shaped building of seven residential levels over ground-floor retail with loft townhouses along 21st Street. It has not started construction; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would require closing on it by 2029-2030.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- no vertical construction is reported on this block (Port Item 11A, Aug 7, 2026: construction of Phase 1 vertical projects and parks has not moved forward, and the developer has not exercised an option on any Phase 1 option parcel). It has not been matched to a specific Assessor lot: DataSF's Assessor layer shows the 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots (blocks 4052 and 4110-4117, mostly added 2019-02-07, most with no street address) and Port Item 12B (Feb 2020) gives Parcel E2 as Block 4116 Lot 008, so which lot, if any, corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map. Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free fit of the plan figure to the map -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this fit's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data. How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Not matched to a specific Assessor lot. DataSF's Assessor layer shows the Pier 70 28-acre site re-mapped into many active P70-MU lots in blocks 4052 and 4110-4117 (mostly added 2019-02-07), so the earlier statement that it has not been subdivided is withdrawn; which lot corresponds to this block has not been checked against the recorded final map, so this record uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential (studio-3BR over 7 levels) + ground-floor retail + townhouses along 21st St, designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, per the architect's own project page (saitowitz.com/pier-70-parcel-d): 'loft town houses along 21st street. Above are studio, one, two and three bedroom units stacked on seven levels', with a retail space along the grove, Market Square and Maryland Street. A weak secondary source implied a ~2020 completion, which no primary source supports: Port Item 11A (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) says construction of Phase 1 vertical projects has not moved forward and that no Phase 1 option parcel has been exercised. The Real Deal (Jul 16, 2026) reports Brookfield's development VP saying additional density would let the company 'break ground in 2027 on its first market-rate apartment building' (350 units, parcel not named), a conditional plan not specific to Parcel D. Treat as NOT yet built.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the Port's Item 11A staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026, for the Aug 11, 2026 meeting), which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Unit count, square footage and the date of the Saitowitz design are not stated on the architect's page and no Planning vertical design approval for Parcel D is listed on the Planning Department's Pier 70 page.
A secondary source implying a ~2020 completion is noted on this parcel's map shape; no primary source supports it, and Port Item 11A says Phase 1 vertical construction has not moved forward.
